metadata.title: How to Read a Three-Card Tarot Spread Without Fixed Positions
metadata.description: Use a no-position three-card tarot method to connect evidence, alternatives, unknowns, and one reversible next step.

three-card-tarot-reading.title: A complete three-card tarot reading without past-present-future positions
three-card-tarot-reading.intro: A three-card spread does not need fixed positions to be specific. Read each upright card as one piece of evidence, compare how the meanings interact, then turn the pattern into alternatives you can check in real life.

sections.heading: What a no-position spread changes
paragraphs: In a fixed spread, the first card may be called the past and the third the future. A no-position spread makes a smaller claim: the numbers record draw order only. Meaning comes from the approved upright meanings and the relationship among them, not from an invented timeline.

This approach is useful when a question has missing information. It keeps the reading reflective: cards can suggest a tension or a useful distinction, but they cannot verify another person's thoughts, guarantee an outcome, or replace evidence.

sections.heading: The six-step method
paragraphs: Work through the spread in this order. Write one or two sentences per step before expanding anything.
items: Question: name the decision or pattern you can influence, and set a time or situation boundary.
Evidence: paraphrase the supplied upright meaning of every card without adding image details or position roles.
Connection: identify the strongest reinforcement, tension, progression, or integration among at least two cards.
Alternatives: write at least two plausible explanations for the same pattern instead of choosing one story too early.
Check: name one observable fact that would make either explanation more likely, and state what is still unknown.
Choice: take one small, reversible action with a stop condition, then ask what you learned before taking a larger step.

sections.heading: Weak question versus workable question
paragraphs: Weak: “Will this relationship definitely work?” This asks the cards to certify another person and a future result.

Workable: “What pattern can I observe in our communication this month, what remains unknown, and what respectful boundary can I test?” The second question creates something the reader can compare with behavior.

sections.heading: Worked example: The Lovers, Two of Swords, The Star
paragraphs: Question: “What should I examine before deciding whether to rebuild trust?” No temporal or advice positions are assigned.

Evidence: The Lovers points to connection, aligned values, and a responsible choice. Two of Swords points to indecision caused by missing information or unclear criteria. The Star points to renewed hope, recovery, and honest trust after difficulty.

Connection: choice and hope reinforce the possibility of repair, while indecision creates a tension: hope alone is not a decision criterion. All three cards contribute to that reading; none is treated as a prediction.
items: Alternative A: trust is rebuilding, but both people need an explicit standard for what repair looks like.
Alternative B: hope is carrying more weight than current behavior, so the decision remains unclear.
Observable discriminator: look for a specific promise followed by consistent behavior, not intensity of words alone.
Unknown: the cards cannot establish the other person's private intention or whether consistency will continue.
Reversible action: ask for one concrete agreement for the next week; pause if the boundary is dismissed or pressured.

sections.heading: How to avoid a generic three-card answer
paragraphs: Do not write three isolated mini-definitions and call them a reading. The useful work is the connection: explain which exact meanings support the pattern, where they disagree, and what observation could change your conclusion.
Length is not the quality target. A shorter answer can be complete when every card contributes, alternatives are materially different, uncertainty is explicit, and the next step can be reversed.

sections.heading: Completion checklist
paragraphs: Before using or sharing the reading, check each condition.
items: Every drawn card appears and is grounded in its supplied upright meaning.
No image, reversed meaning, hidden-feelings claim, timeline, or fixed position was invented.
At least one relationship among cards is explained with evidence.
At least two alternatives and one observable discriminator are present.
Unknowns are separated from interpretations.
The action is small, reversible, and includes a reason to pause.

metadata.title: How to Ask Tarot Questions: From Prediction to Reflection
metadata.description: Rewrite yes-no and hidden-feelings tarot questions into specific, observable, agency-centered questions with examples.

how-to-ask-tarot-questions.title: How to ask tarot questions that lead to useful reflection
how-to-ask-tarot-questions.intro: A strong tarot question does not ask a symbolic tool to prove a fact. It defines what you can observe, what you can choose, and what uncertainty must remain open.

sections.heading: The four boundaries of a strong question
paragraphs: Use tarot to organize attention, not to obtain private information or professional advice. A workable question stays inside four boundaries.
items: Agency: focus on your choices, communication, preparation, or boundary.
Observability: ask what behavior, evidence, or criterion you can actually check.
Uncertainty: leave room for more than one explanation and name what the cards cannot establish.
Scope: limit the question to a situation or near-term review point instead of an unlimited future.

sections.heading: A reusable question formula
paragraphs: Use: “What pattern should I examine in [situation], what evidence would distinguish the main alternatives, and what small choice can I test before [review point]?”
The formula is not magic wording. Its value is structural: it forces interpretation, evidence, alternatives, and action to remain separate.

sections.heading: Prediction-to-reflection rewrites
items: Instead of “Does my ex still love me?” ask “What evidence would show that renewed contact is mutual, respectful, and different from the old pattern?”
Instead of “Will I get the job?” ask “What can I strengthen before the interview, what hiring factors remain outside my control, and when should I reassess?”
Instead of “Is this person lying?” ask “Which inconsistencies can I verify directly, and what boundary protects me while the facts are unclear?”
Instead of “When will money improve?” ask “Which spending or income assumption should I review with real records, and which decision needs qualified financial advice?”
Instead of “What is my destiny?” ask “Which value deserves more weight in the next reversible choice?”

sections.heading: Worked example: The Tower, Eight of Pentacles, Temperance
paragraphs: Starting question: “Will this career setback ruin my future?” Rewrite: “Which assumption did the setback expose, which skill can I improve, and how can I balance recovery with a practical next attempt?”

Evidence: The Tower means disruption that exposes assumptions and requires an honest reset, not a prediction of disaster. Eight of Pentacles points to skill improving through consistent practice. Temperance points to patiently balancing and integrating different needs.

Connection: The Tower and Eight of Pentacles form a reset-to-practice progression, while Temperance prevents practice from becoming a rushed attempt to erase the setback. Together, the cards frame the decision as learning from exposed assumptions while balancing recovery with deliberate skill-building.

Two alternatives now become possible: the setback may reveal a preparation gap that practice can address, or the role itself may conflict with a need that was previously ignored. The discriminator is concrete feedback from the application or work sample, not the emotional force of the setback.
items: Unknown: whether a particular employer will make an offer.
Reversible action: request one specific piece of feedback and schedule one short practice block.
Stop condition: do not keep applying the same strategy if repeated feedback points to a different constraint.

sections.heading: Questions that should leave tarot
paragraphs: Medical symptoms, legal duties, financial or investment decisions, mental-health crises, and immediate safety risks need appropriate evidence and qualified help. Tarot may support journaling about feelings, but it should not decide diagnosis, treatment, liability, investment, or emergency action.
If a question involves coercion, stalking, self-harm, or danger, prioritize safety and real support rather than another draw.

sections.heading: Question checklist
items: Can I answer part of this question through my own observation or choice?
Does it avoid claiming access to another person's hidden mind?
Does it allow at least two plausible explanations?
Does it name evidence or a review point?
Is the next action small enough to reverse?
Have I moved professional or safety decisions outside tarot?

metadata.title: How to Read Tarot Card Combinations Without Memorizing Pairs
metadata.description: Learn four meaning-grounded tarot combination relationships and work through a complete three-card example.

tarot-card-combinations.title: How to read tarot card combinations without a fixed pair dictionary
tarot-card-combinations.intro: A card combination is not a secret phrase attached to two names. It is a relationship you can explain between the supplied upright meanings in this particular question.

sections.heading: Four useful relationship types
paragraphs: Choose the relationship that best fits the meanings; do not force every pair into a story.
items: Reinforcement: two meanings point toward the same need, resource, or risk.
Tension: the meanings pull toward competing needs or expose a tradeoff.
Progression: one meaning describes a condition that makes another response useful, without turning draw order into a timeline.
Integration: the meanings become more useful when both are held together instead of choosing one.

sections.heading: The evidence sentence
paragraphs: Write the connection as: “Because [meaning A] and [meaning B], the spread may be asking us to compare [specific pattern].” Then quote or paraphrase the exact parts of both meanings that support the claim.
If you cannot finish that sentence without image symbolism, a fixed position, or outside card lore, the connection is not grounded enough yet.

sections.heading: Worked example: Five of Cups, Two of Wands, The Hermit
paragraphs: Question: “What will help me choose a direction after a disappointing project?” Five of Cups points to acknowledging loss and working through disappointment. Two of Wands points to planning and choosing a direction. The Hermit points to stepping back and reflecting on your own guidance.

Strongest connection—progression, not chronology: disappointment needs acknowledgment before planning becomes honest, and quiet reflection can supply a personal criterion for the plan. This does not mean the cards occupy past, present, and future positions.
items: Alternative A: the next direction is unclear because disappointment has not been named precisely.
Alternative B: the loss is understood, but too many outside opinions are replacing a personal decision criterion.
Observable discriminator: write what failed, then see whether a direction emerges from that evidence or only after outside approval.
Unknown: which new project will succeed.

Reversible action and stop condition: spend twenty minutes making two criteria and compare one small trial against them. Stop and revise the criteria if the trial supplies no relevant evidence or only repeats the same outside approval you meant to test.

sections.heading: How to handle three or six cards
paragraphs: With three cards, identify one strongest connection and one meaningful tension if it exists. With six cards, group the meanings into two or three semantic clusters before comparing them. Do not explain all fifteen possible pairs; that usually creates repetition rather than insight.
A card can contribute to more than one cluster, but every card must contribute somewhere. If one card is ignored, revise the synthesis instead of attaching a generic sentence at the end.

sections.heading: Combination mistakes to avoid
items: Treating draw order as past-present-future without an explicitly chosen spread.
Using a memorized pair meaning that contradicts the supplied upright meanings.
Inventing colors, figures, directions, or reversed meanings when no image or reversal was provided.
Turning court cards into literal people, genders, ages, or professions.
Listing every pair while never stating the strongest overall pattern.
Collapsing ambiguity into one prediction instead of testing alternatives.

sections.heading: Combination checklist
items: The relationship type is named and supported by exact meanings.
Every card contributes to the synthesis.
The interpretation fits the question without inventing personal facts.
At least two alternatives are materially different.
One observable cue could distinguish those alternatives.
Unknowns and a reversible next step are explicit.

metadata.title: About tarot-spark
metadata.description: Learn what tarot-spark is, how the free tarot prompt generator works, and what boundaries apply.

about.title: About tarot-spark
about.intro: tarot-spark is a free tarot card drawing and AI prompt generator for reflective writing.

sections.heading: What this site does
paragraphs: You can choose a topic, reading depth, and style, add optional situation context, and copy a prompt that helps you write about the result in an AI tool.
The experience is built for entertainment, journaling, and self-reflection rather than prediction or professional advice.

sections.heading: How the readings work
paragraphs: Each draw uses local tarot card and spread data. The site does not ask for your name, birth date, contact details, or a personal question.
The generated prompt is meant to help you explore symbols and possible perspectives. You decide what is useful and what to ignore.

sections.heading: How guide content is made
paragraphs: The guides start from tarot-spark's reviewed nonvisual upright meanings. Examples separate card evidence, interpretation, unknowns, alternative explanations, observable checks, and reversible choices. They do not use image details, reversed meanings, fixed positions, or claims about hidden feelings unless a page explicitly explains why those claims are unsupported.

We review Korean and English pages for the same method and example coverage before publishing them. Material corrections update the page directly instead of preserving numbered content editions. Feedback can be sent to tarotspark.app@gmail.com.

metadata.title: Privacy Policy | tarot-spark
metadata.description: Read how tarot-spark handles analytics, advertising, browser features, and contact messages.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what tarot-spark collects and how the site is designed to avoid personal tarot inputs.

sections.heading: Information you provide
paragraphs: tarot-spark does not require an account. If you add optional situation or relationship context, do not include names, birth dates, contact details, workplace secrets, or other information that identifies a person.

Optional context stays in your browser and is omitted from reading URLs and analytics. A one-time same-tab browser handoff preserves it when you switch languages or when changing a privacy choice requires the page to reload. It leaves the site only when you choose to copy the generated prompt and paste or share it elsewhere.
If you email tarotspark.app@gmail.com, the email address and message content you send are used to read and respond to your message.

sections.heading: Analytics
paragraphs: When Google Analytics is enabled, the site may collect page views and behavior events such as topic clicks, card draws, result views, prompt copies, and share clicks.

Analytics payloads are limited to stable event details such as locale, topic id, card count, card ids, and the stable id of a selected public question preset. Localized question text, names, birth dates, contact details, personal free-form questions, and optional situation text are not included.

sections.heading: Browser features
paragraphs: Prompt copy and share actions use browser clipboard or share features. The prompt text stays in your browser unless you choose to copy, share, or paste it elsewhere.
Instant readings are available only when a separate server setting is enabled. When this feature is off, card data is not sent to an external generative AI service.

sections.heading: Third-party services
paragraphs: The site may be hosted on Vercel. When the corresponding services and identifiers are enabled, Google Analytics and Google AdSense remain off until you allow those optional services in the privacy choices. Advertising delivery may also be disabled site-wide. When enabled, AdSense loads only on the reviewed relationship content pages (/relationship-flow, /ko/relationship-flow, /relationship-tarot-questions, and /ko/relationship-tarot-questions).
Google AdSense and its partners may use cookies or other local storage and process device, page, and ad interaction data to serve, measure, and, where permitted, personalize ads.

When instant readings are available, the selected topic, card count, answer tone, tarot-spark's predefined nonvisual upright meanings, and—if one was chosen—the predefined public reflection-question focus are sent in input order to the Google Gemini API to create the interpretation. Card names, card images, invented position meanings, optional situation text, names, birth dates, contact details, and personal free-form questions are not sent. Requests are configured not to be stored, but Google may process requests and results under the applicable terms and project settings.

Your optional-service choices are stored in this browser and can be revised through the Privacy choices control. Those providers process technical, analytics, and advertising data according to their own terms and privacy policies.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: For privacy questions or deletion requests related to emails you sent, contact tarotspark.app@gmail.com.
Last updated: July 31, 2026.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: Use email for feedback, privacy questions, or site issues related to tarot-spark.

sections.heading: Email
paragraphs: Send messages to tarotspark.app@gmail.com.
Include the page or feature you are referring to when reporting a site issue.

sections.heading: Response scope
paragraphs: tarot-spark can respond to product feedback, accessibility issues, privacy questions, and bug reports.
Do not use this contact channel for urgent medical, legal, financial, investment, mental-health, or safety decisions.

metadata.description: Read the entertainment and self-reflection disclaimer for tarot-spark.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: tarot-spark is for entertainment and self-reflection only.

sections.heading: No professional advice
paragraphs: Tarot content, prompts, card meanings, and reflections on this site are not medical, legal, financial, investment, mental-health, or other professional advice.
Do not rely on tarot-spark for decisions that require a qualified professional.

sections.heading: No guaranteed outcomes
paragraphs: Tarot interpretations are symbolic and subjective. They may be incomplete, inaccurate, or not useful for your situation.
You are responsible for how you use, copy, share, or interpret generated prompts.

sections.heading: Use boundaries
paragraphs: If a topic involves safety, health, legal obligations, money, investments, or emotional crisis, seek appropriate professional support instead of relying on tarot content.
The site is intended for general reflection, creative writing, and light personal insight.
